page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.sn2ne.8xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 32 dedicated physical cores on the x86_64 architecture, utilizing an Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor operating at a clock speed of 2.5 GHz. The CPU configuration provides 32 vCPUs with a single thread per core and includes 35 MB of L3 cache. The instance is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, and it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 6 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates a clear performance tradeoff between single-core and multi-core execution. Single-core performance is relatively weak, with stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the bottom 25%, and single-threaded gzip compression performing in the bottom 10%. However, multi-core benchmarks show average performance, with the Geekbench multi-core score reaching 8272.0 and the PassMark CPU score at 23181.17. Memory bandwidth tests also demonstrate average capabilities, with read-only large block bandwidth at 98.48 GB/sec and write large block bandwidth at 49.01 GB/sec.

Given the dedicated CPU allocation and balanced resource ratio, this instance is suited for multi-threaded workloads that do not rely heavily on high single-core clock speeds. Appropriate workloads include static web serving, database operations, and software compilation, which align with its average multi-threaded benchmark results. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the hardware profile offers a stable, dedicated resource density for legacy enterprise applications and general-purpose computing, though workloads requiring high single-threaded throughput or local NVMe storage will face performance limitations.

The instance has a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, 6 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth, and no local storage or GPU hardware. Performance benchmarks reveal a distinct tradeoff: single-core capabilities are weak, falling in the bottom 25% for Geekbench and stress-ng, while multi-core performance is average, as evidenced by a PassMark CPU score of 23181.17 and a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression speed of 109.42 GB/sec. This hardware profile is suited for multi-threaded general-purpose workloads, including database operations, static web serving, and software compilation, offering a stable dedicated resource allocation for enterprise applications.
